title: A Second Life for Old Chairs
transcript: We spoke to furniture repairer Daniel Hart at his Saturday workshop. I asked how he learnt to fix wooden chairs. 'My neighbour showed me when I was fifteen,' he said. 'She made me practise on a broken chair from her shed.' When I asked what customers usually get wrong, Daniel pointed to a loose leg. 'People put in a bigger screw, but that can split the wood,' he said. His advice is to bring the chair in before trying to fix it at home.

questions.prompt: Who first taught Daniel to fix chairs?
questions.explanation: 丹尼尔十五岁时，一位邻居教他修椅子。

questions.prompt: What does Daniel advise people to do?
options: Take the legs off at home.
Bring the chair in before trying to fix it.
questions.answer: Bring the chair in before trying to fix it.
questions.explanation: 最后建议在家动手前先把椅子带到工坊。
